newsitem.title: UK: Summary of economic/political views on UK budget.
newsitem.headline: Summary of economic/political views on UK budget.

text.p: Following is a selection of comments from analysts and politicians after Britain's ruling Labour party delivered its first budget since 1978.
PAUL MORTIMER-LEE, CHIEF CAPITAL MARKETS ECONOMIST AT PARIBAS CAPITAL MARKETS
"He's not going to kill the economy, he's going to let it continue to grow."
CONSERVATIVE LEADER WILLIAM HAGUE

"This is a tax raising budget. When the Chancellor says he is tightening fiscal policy by 5-3/4 billion (pounds), he means he is introducing a tax raising budget. It is clear that this budget delivers a double whammy against pensions."
JIM STRIDE, DIRECTOR OF SUN LIFE INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT

"Keeping the spending under control is the key issue as far as the City (London's financial district) is concerned and I think they have done it... It has been very carefully structured to minimise the adverse impact on the retail price index. All in all it is a very clever package."
VICKY PRYCE, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT KPMG

"Looking ahead, export order books are declining and confidence is at an all time low. This is going to remain a problem. They haven't tackled the consumer side. Sterling will remain strong and that's a worry."
DAVID EDDY, CHIEF FOREX DEALER AT SUMITOMO

"Interest rates are going up without a doubt and, given the outlook for continental Europe, you have to be looking for a move to 2.95 marks (which was sterling's old Exchange Rate Mechanism midpoint) and above."
STEPHEN HANNAH, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT IBJ

"It (the budget deficit projection) certainly puts the UK back in line with its European partners and will be beneficial to the gilt market once the threat of significantly higher interest rates has passed."
PADDY ASHDOWN, LIBERAL DEMOCRAT LEADER
"Instead of shackling businesses, he should have restrained the consumer in order to prevent the higher interest rates (and) higher inflation...that in our view will now surely follow."
MARK RAMSDEN, ECONOMIST AT STONE AND MCCARTHY RESEARCH ASSOCIATES

"I will still be looking for a rate rise probably in August, possibly in July. I think the Chancellor has decided to leave the management of the business cycle to the Bank of England and concentrate on structural reforms."
BRIAN HILLIARD, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT SOCIETE GENERALE

"In terms of tightening it's encouraging. But we need to know how quickly these tax changes kick in. Taken at face value - the tightening is more than the City expected and should take some pressure off interest rates."
FORMER CONSERVATIVE CHANCELLOR OF THE EXCHEQUER KENNETH CLARKE
"This is a big tightening of policy budget. He hasn't hit the ordinary voter too much. He hasn't hit consumer taxes in any very unexpected way...he has hit the corporate sector.
"He is trying to get a free lunch out of the windfall tax, he's gone for the biggest possible hit on that."
- London newsroom **4471 542 6784
